speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I'm Dr. Agent. Can you describe the rash on your scalp and forehead, specifically noting if it is itchy, painful, or scaly?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the rash extend to the diaper area or other skin folds, and have you noticed any crusting or "cradle cap" on the scalp? I would also like to know if the baby has had any recent ear infections or if the rash seems to worsen after feeding.

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of greasy yellow scales on the scalp and forehead in a 3-month-old infant is highly characteristic of infantile seborrheic dermatitis, commonly known as cradle cap. I will proceed with the diagnosis based on these classic clinical findings. DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis
